recentItems.title: The Art of Great Conversations | Olivia Kinghorst | TEDxEHL Lausanne
recentItems.description:
Olivia Kinghorst brings her experience as an international moderator onto the TEDx stage sharing her most valuable insights on the industry and what makes a good public speaker. Through personal experience as well as societal truths, Olivia brings a fresh perspective for the younger generation of speakers to better understand the art of great conversations.  Olivia Kinghorst is an international moderator, Master of Ceremonies and
keynote speaker. She was a former anchor for CNN Money Switzerland and Senior Editor at Forbes Switzerland. She has been invited to host and speak on some of the world's biggest stages including the World Economic Forum, Cannes Lions, Web Summit, Mobile World Congress, Nordic Business Forum and Forbes Women's Summit. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What looks good on paper | Quentin Fantoli | TEDxEHL Lausanne
recentItems.description: In his TEDx talk, he challenges the idea that success is simply what looks good on paper, exploring the tension between academic achievement, athletic ambition and personal health, and reminding us that true success means knowing when to listen to our bodies rather than constantly chasing performance. Quentin Fantoli is a triathlete and entrepreneur, co-founder of MO-WA, where health, sport, and business performance meet. A top graduate of EHL, he was ranked 2nd best student and received the EHL Spirit Award, before completing a master's at AISTS. He later chose to step off the conventional path and pursue triathlon full-time with Tribu Performance, building MO-WA alongside his wife, Lisa. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Why Asking For Love Makes It Real | Aurélien Henry | TEDxEHL Lausanne
recentItems.description: Aurélien Henry discusses a rule almost nobody has ever said out loud: "if I had anything to do with it then it doesn't count". He explains that this rule is why a compliment you ask for, dies in your hands, and why some people starve for love in a room that is full of it. This talk takes that rule apart, and argues that the proof you have been waiting for was never going to arrive, because there has never been a version of you that somebody could love without you having built it first.  Aurélien Henry is a current Bosc 3 student studying at EHL. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Grandma Knew That: Reclaiming Ancestral Wellness Wisdom | Nnenna Uneke | TEDxWilliam James College
recentItems.description: We were taught to call our grandmothers’ daily rituals primitive. Then the world rediscovered them, renamed them, and sold them back to us. This talk is an invitation to take a second look at the healing that was always ours. Nnenna Uneke is a doctoral candidate in organizational leadership psychology, a certified trauma therapist, consultant, and founder of Integrative Wellbeing Center. She is building NurtXure, a supervision platform for therapists, and designs corporate wellbeing programs. Rooted in African tradition and indigenous healing, she trains therapists across Africa and the diaspora, and those serving African communities. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: 5 Pasos Para Diseñar tu Vida y Transformar tu Destino | Abraham J. Lopez | TEDxWilmington Salon
recentItems.description:
Como sociedad, tendemos a enfocarnos en las debilidades cognitivas de las personas, y al hacer esto, restringimos sus oportunidades para obtener el éxito, afectamos su funcionamiento emocional, social, financiero, y relacional. En esta charla TEDx, el Dr. Abraham Lopez, Ph.D., neuropsicólogo clínico, nos comparte:
#1. Una mejor manera de pensar para mejorar la autoestima y asegurar una mejor vida, sin importar los retos o contextos culturales
#2. Pasos importantes para evitar la vergüenza y humillación y crear confianza y conexión, y #3. 
5 preguntas que nos ayudarán a superar prácticamente cualquier desafío, ya sea cognitivo, social o cultural.
 Nacido en El Paso, Texas, de padres inmigrantes mexicanos, el Dr. Abraham J. López es neuropsicólogo clínico y cofundador de LarLo Behavioral en El Paso. Vivió con TDAH sin diagnóstico hasta los 38 años, repitiendo dos grados escolares antes de descubrir, ya en su carrera, que podía redirigir esa misma mente hacia sus fortalezas. Ese cambio de enfoque lo llevó a obtener dos maestrías y un doctorado en tiempo récord, convirtiéndose en el primero de su generación académica en certificarse como psicólogo clínico. Hoy es profesor clínico asistente en Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center El Paso y evalúa a niños en El Paso Children’s Hospital. Le apasiona hacer accesible la ciencia del cerebro a las comunidades históricamente desatendidas en las que creció, y transformar cómo hablamos de la neurodivergencia, de lo que está mal en el cerebro a lo que está bien. Para más información, visita LarLoBehavioral.com y conéctate con el Dr. Abraham J. López en LinkedIn. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Be a Hero: Wear the Change | Elvira Zamora | TEDxInglewood
recentItems.description:
What if changing the world started with what's already in your closet?

Fashion designer Elvira Zamora challenges us to rethink our relationship with clothing and the environmental impact of fast fashion. Drawing from her Peruvian heritage, her father's influence as a tailor, and her journey into sustainable fashion, Elvira shares how creativity and conscious choices can help reduce waste without sacrificing personal style.

Through the art of upcycling, she explores how we can give new life to existing clothing, embrace secondhand and vintage fashion, and use our purchasing power to create meaningful change.

Her message is a reminder that sustainability doesn't have to mean giving up what we love. Sometimes, making a difference begins with reimagining what we already have. Elvira Zamora is a fashion designer, creative entrepreneur, and accountability coach whose work blends Indigenous culture, sustainable fashion, and intentional design. Born in Peru, she immigrated to Los Angeles at age 10 and grew up in the San Fernando Valley, where her creative journey began.

Coming from a family of fashion creatives, Elvira launched her first fashion business in her father's tailor shop in 2001. What began as a small women's boutique has evolved into a gender-free fashion brand specializing in one-of-a-kind, upcycled designs that celebrate cultural identity and individuality.

Through her work, Elvira challenges conventional perceptions of fashion by creating garments that tell stories, honor Indigenous traditions, and incorporate sustainable practices. Her designs combine traditional influences with contemporary aesthetics, emphasizing cultural authenticity, ethical production, and the importance of creating with purpose.

Beyond fashion, Elvira is an accountability coach who helps creatives and entrepreneurs develop clarity, discipline, and sustainable practices in their personal and professional lives. She is also committed to philanthropy and supporting underserved communities.

Across her work, Elvira advocates for creativity that honors cultural heritage, encourages intentional living, and demonstrates how fashion can serve as a meaningful form of personal and cultural expression. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: It’s Not in Your Head - It’s in Your Blood | Dr. Dominika Repcikova | TEDxCoolhaven Women
recentItems.description: Why women’s exhaustion and anxiety can have an overlooked biological dimension, and why building products around women’s biology starts with asking better questions and measuring what we too often miss - including something as fundamental as iron deficiency. Dominika is a scientist and founder working at the intersection of women’s health, biology and data. As founder and CEO of The Iron Bar, she is confronting one of women’s most normalised health crises: iron deficiency. Her talk will explore how the problem became so widely accepted and what building a better solution actually takes. recentItems.title: Mom, Can I Download Tinder? | Katherine Gyolai | TEDxMinneapolis
recentItems.description: What if protecting someone from getting hurt also prevents them from finding love? Adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities deserve the same opportunities for connection, romance, and meaningful relationships as anyone else. Yet fear of exploitation often leads families, caregivers, and communities to avoid conversations about dating, consent, and intimacy altogether. Katherine Gyolai, founder of Find Love Safely and mother and stepmother to eight adult children, four with intellectual or developmental disabilities, challenges us to reconsider what protection really means. She reveals why relationship education—not avoidance—is essential to helping adults recognize healthy connections, establish boundaries, make informed choices, and pursue love more safely. Her message challenges a common assumption: We don’t protect people by denying them the opportunity to love. We empower them by giving them the tools to pursue it safely. Filmed August 4, 2026, at Orchestra Hall in Minneapolis. A mom, community leader, and founder of a Twin Cities organization serving adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities, Katherine is advocating for a cultural shift that starts right here. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Unheard Superpower: The Voice That Says “Not Yet” | Anil Panicker | TEDxKIT Coimbatore
recentItems.description: Success is seen, but adversity is unseen. Anil Panicker shows how hard times can reveal the strength already within us, and why the voice that says “not yet” matters more than the one that says “you can’t”. Anil Panicker is an accomplished professional with an MBA in Marketing and over 30 years of extensive Corporate Leadership Experience. He wears multiple hats as an Adversity Quotient (AQ) specialist, Leadership & Faculty Development trainer, Certified Career Mentor, and Vedic Numerologist. He is also the author of the book Born to Rise – Reborn to Shine, he also shares his insights as a YouTuber, hosting a channel with over 200 leadership and life quality enhancing videos. Throughout his career, he has successfully empowered more than 4,000 professionals and mentored upwards of 300 students, guiding them to unlock their potential and effectively thrive through adversity. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Sibling Story | Subashri V | TEDxKIT Coimbatore
recentItems.description: Subashri Vasudevan spent her childhood trying to be the opposite of her brother, until a phone call at her lowest point turned into 30+ co-authored books together. A warm story of sibling rivalry, second chances, and why we become who we watch. Subashri is an Assistant Vice President at Bank of America Continuum India, Chennai, with over a decade of experience in software engineering, and enterprise ETL solutions. She has built large-scale data pipeline and integration solutions across banking and financial services, working extensively with Azure Data Factory, Azure Synapse Analytics, SSIS, and SQL Server. A Microsoft Community Champion, Intel Innovator, and Google Women Tech Maker, she combines deep technical expertise with active community leadership. A published author of 20 books spanning Deep Learning, Software Engineering, Digital Electronics, & Computer Networking,  published by Taylor & Francis, Wiley, Alpha Science International, and Narosa, she is also a patent holder and hackathon winner with 15+ victories at national and international platforms. She holds the unique distinction of being a World Record holder alongside her sibling, recognized as the only siblings globally to have co-authored 15 books together. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: In an AI World, Let’s Become Intentionally Human | Pallavi Narayan | TEDxKIT Coimbatore
recentItems.description:
Machines have learnt to speak like us, but they aren’t us, so the real question is no longer “why AI” but “who is answerable?” Pallavi Narayan explores six hard questions AI forces on us, from bias and deepfakes to the hidden cost of every prompt, and makes the case for becoming intentionally human. Pallavi Narayan is a pioneering voice at the intersection of Industrial AI and Energy, with over 25 years of experience transforming how the energy sector thinks, operates, and innovates. As an Energy Industry SME and Innovation Lead at Accenture, she has been at the forefront of designing and deploying GenAI and Agentic AI powered solutions that redefine industrial operations, from asset management and water management platforms to retail operations transformation and AI powered refinery solutions. 
A cross-functional leader who has driven end to end value creation across Product Strategy, Services Delivery, Pre-Sales, Sales, and Innovation CoE, Pallavi brings a rare combination of instrumentation engineering roots, cloud architecture expertise, and AI leadership that gives her a uniquely grounded perspective on Industrial AI, not just as a technology, but as a business reinvention engine. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
